subject.title: Workboard: improve stacked-card readability and human-approval visibility

question: Should Workboard represent human-approval/action-required cards as a first-class UI state, a configurable prominent-label rule, or leave the current blocked/status/label conventions unchanged?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable product contract is not: a fix could be UI-only, metadata-driven, or a new plugin config surface, and repository policy sets a high bar for new config/default behavior.

options.title: Add UI-local human-action signal
options.body: Use existing Workboard status, metadata, notes, or labels to surface an attention affordance/count without creating plugin config unless later proven necessary.

options.title: Add configurable prominent labels
options.body: Define a plugin-owned config contract for approval-needed label patterns, with docs and tests for the new user-visible configuration surface.

options.title: Keep current conventions
options.body: Document blocked status, labels, and filters as the supported path and close or narrow the enhancement after maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Add UI-local human-action signal
recommendation.body: Use existing Workboard status, metadata, notes, or labels to surface an attention affordance/count without creating plugin config unless later proven necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest history-backed owner for Workboard product-surface direction and optional plugin configuration.
